text:
lucy_support: FYI — ACME tenant (tenant_id: acme-14) reported 429s + big tail latency on Dedicated pool D-42 starting ~2026-02-26 03:10 UTC. They say "requests started failing during ingest batch" and that autoscale didn't add nodes.

lucy_support: Paste of client error they sent:
```
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","code":429,"request_id":"req_8f3a2b","message":"tenant quota exceeded: requests_per_min limit reached"}
```

autoscale-bot: [autoscale-event] 2026-02-26T03:05:12Z scale_down complete (2 -> 1 replicas). reason=low_queue
autoscale-bot: [autoscale-event] 2026-02-26T03:12:03Z scale_up prevented: tenant rate limit blocking new work (tenant=acme-14)

tim_sre: Can we get the tenant quota config and the pool-level rate caps? This sounds like a per-tenant requests_per_min vs tokens_per_min misalignment we saw last month.

maya_eng: Checked the tenant config in config-service: `quota_unit":"tokens_per_min"` but the rate limiting middleware reads `requests_per_min`. The stored values for acme-14 are `limit: 5000` which the system interprets as 5000 tokens/min but rate limiter treats as 5000 req/min -> huge mismatch when avg tokens/req ~120 -> effectively 120x overcap.

lucy_support: Oof. So the quota looked permissive but actually became very strict for request counts. I've applied a temporary support override to the tenant to 200 req/min while we fix mapping. billing_bot shows event:
```
{event: "quota_override", actor: "lucy_support", tenant: "acme-14", new_limit: "200 requests_per_min", ts: "2026-02-26T03:20:45Z"}
```

tim_sre: Thanks. For repro I want a small load loop that mimics their ingestion: 1) POST 6MB batches every 500ms with 120 tokens per request average. Run from staging using tenant creds. Example k6 snippet:
```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function(){
  http.post('https://staging.redwood.example/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({input: 'x'.repeat(6*1024*1024)}), {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer STAGING_ACME_KEY'}});
  sleep(0.5);
}
```

maya_eng: Also add this check to confirm the limiter's interpreted unit:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer SVC_TOKEN" https://internal-config/tenants/acme-14 | jq .quota
```
Expect `{"unit":"tokens_per_min","limit":5000}`. If limiter is reading as requests_per_min we need hotfix in middleware to respect unit field.

lucy_support: Customer confirmed errors stopped after override. They're asking for RCA and timeline. I'll tell them we're patching mapping and will follow up.

tim_sre: I'll open a quick PR to the rate-limiter to add unit sanity checks and a soft-fail that logs mismatch and falls back to token-based calculation. tagging @maya_eng for review. Also create postmortem once patch deploys.

maya_eng: Filed ENG-PR-1129, test plan attached. We'll also add a CI test that writes a tenant with tokens_per_min unit and ensures limiter interprets correctly.

lucy_support: Thanks team. I'll keep customer updated. :thumbsup:
